A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DAIL research despite the changed title. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, figures and tables, are readable and support reliable matching across versions.

before.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B report original DAIL and baseline evaluations on mathematics and GPQA, including efficiency, ablation and generalization results.

after.justification: The empirical studies are retained and revised, with additional non-mathematics evaluations, model configurations, distillation comparisons and exploratory experiments.

M1.justification: The main mixed-policy generation procedure and contrastive KL objective remain unchanged; 'privileged student' is renamed 'teacher'. Limited extensions appear in the exploratory on-policy DAIL variant in Appendix C.7 and HealthBench teacher conditioning on both expert solutions and grading rubrics in Appendix B.

E1.justification: The mathematics training and mathematics/GPQA evaluation coverage is retained. Appendix B adds training and evaluation on Maze and Rotten Oranges from Reasoning Gym, healthcare responses through HealthBench, and tool calling through Tool Alpaca, substantially broadening task and domain coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix C.8 and Table 10 add supervised distillation from Qwen3-235B-A22B (think) as an evaluated comparator. The original SFT, STaR and RLVR comparator memberships remain; applying existing baselines to the new domains does not itself constitute another comparator addition.

E3.justification: Appendix C.1 explicitly reports rerunning test-time evaluations with an added final-answer prompt to address non-response. The reported e1-verifiable RL settings change from 15 GRPO epochs plus 15 NuRL epochs to 5 plus 5, and rollout temperature changes from 0.6 to 1.0. New experiments also introduce Qwen3-14B and Llama configurations, a distillation comparison controlling tokens per example, and GPT-4o-mini grading for HealthBench.

E4.justification: The revision substantially extends capability and backbone analyses through Qwen3-14B scaling, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct failure testing and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B evaluation. Appendix C.7 adds a qualitative investigation of slow on-policy convergence, while Figure 16 revises the smaller-model analysis. Existing loss, sampling and deduplication analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The 128-sample pass@k estimation practice is retained. Neither version reports training-seed replication, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests; the added experiments introduce no new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: RL results change in Figures 2, 6 and 14, and Figures 4 and 16 replace test-time results under revised evaluation conditions. Tables 2–5 and 10–12 add domain, distillation and backbone outcomes. These include HealthBench totals of 0.16 for both base and DAIL, and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct pass@1 of 0.64 versus DAIL's 0.47. GPQA Table 1 and the contrastive-loss ablation values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, mixed-policy acceptance rule, contrastive objective and pass@k estimator are unchanged apart from teacher notation. Neither version supplies additional formal propositions, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract changes the reported gains from 10–25% pass@k to up to 31% pass@128 and narrows the efficiency claim from 2–4 times to twice as efficient. The introduction adds a model-size and test-time scaling claim, while the central contributions remain expert-solution transformation and contrastive learning.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the expanded results as supporting scaling with model size and test-time compute, and acknowledges that offline efficiency may sacrifice performance. Its weaker-model discussion replaces v1's instruction-following, shortcut and gamma-tuning explanations with a capacity-versus-task-difficulty interpretation supported by the added Llama experiment. The central shortcut-learning explanation remains.

D1.justification: v2 documents an RL hyperparameter search, an additional eight-A40 hardware option, the corrected answer prompt, and new tasks' supervision, sample sizes, splits and grader. Core DAIL hyperparameters, mathematical-domain generation prompts and code/data access links are retained.

R1.justification: Section 4 adds Hübotter and Shenfeld's concurrent self-distillation work and repositions the already-cited Zhao work within that discussion. New benchmark citations and Shao et al.'s backbone-generalization motivation are added. These locally extend the positioning without replacing the existing related-work framework.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, consistently replaces 'privileged student' with 'teacher', and makes localized prose corrections and discussion revisions. It adds acknowledgments and a non-mathematics appendix, moving the previous Appendix B details to Appendix C. Most of the main narrative and section order remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 4 expands to six panels with a Qwen3-14B row, and Figure 16 is redrawn, enlarged and relocated. New domain, distillation and backbone tables substantially expand the displays. Table 8 additionally tabulates Figure 2's results; it is a numerical redisplay rather than a separate experiment. Existing prompts and ablation displays are largely retained or relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses an important defect in the central efficiency evaluation: Appendix C.1 reports reducing non-response from over 10% to at most 0.2% through corrected answer prompting and rerunning the experiments, while narrowing the efficiency claim. Added domain, backbone and distillation tests better establish applicability and expose neutral or negative outcomes. Some retained RL-failure language overstates the updated evidence—for example, Table 8 shows GRPO exceeding the base model on AIME pass@128—but the evaluation repair and broader empirical scrutiny provide a substantial net improvement.
